hero.title: Undergraduate Computer Engineering in Ireland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Earn an Engineers Ireland accredited Bachelor of Engineering in Ireland, the premier European semiconductor and electronics hardware hub, accessing top tech multinationals and 12-month Stamp 1G stay-back authorization.

overview: Ireland is home to major European semiconductor fabrication, embedded systems design, and medical device hardware facilities, including Intel's flagship European manufacturing campus and leading multinational electronics design centers. Studying undergraduate Computer Engineering in Ireland places Indian students in close proximity to Europe's most dynamic hardware technology sector.

Irish universities offer 4-year Bachelor of Engineering (BE / BAI, NFQ Level 8) degrees accredited by Engineers Ireland. Core modules include digital logic, microelectronic circuit design, microprocessor architecture, embedded systems, and communication networks, supported by formal industrial work placements (such as DCU INTRA or university cooperative internships) that provide 6 to 9 months of embedded hardware engineering experience.

Under the Irish Government's Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G), eligible international graduates from NFQ Level 8 Honours Bachelor's engineering programs can obtain a 12-month non-renewable post-study work permit to seek skilled employment in Ireland, providing an established pathway toward a Critical Skills Employment Permit across Ireland's thriving semiconductor and advanced electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

sections.title: Why Study Computer Engineering in Ireland?
sections.lead: Ireland has strong engineering, computing and technology programs that attract international students. Its universities provide engineering programs that blend theoretical knowledge with practical lab work, design projects and industry exposure.

items: - Industry opportunities: Ireland has technology, semiconductor, software, telecommunications and medical device companies
Hands-on learning: A lot of courses include hardware labs, engineering projects and industry placements.
International exposure: Students learn with students from different countries and backgrounds.
Career flexibility: Graduates can work in the fields of embedded systems, computer hardware, electronics, robotics and computer networks.
Continuing education: Students can continue to master's degree programs in computer engineering, electronic engineering, artificial intelligence or similar.
Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance helps students to explore these opportunities and understand the requirements to study abroad.

sections.title: Admission Process for Computer Engineering in Ireland

items: The general application process goes like this:

items.title: Research programs. Look for courses covering your chosen subjects like embedded systems, computer hardware or communications engineering.
Check eligibility. Check academic requirements, English-language requirements, course length, and accepted international qualifications.
Get your documents together. Gather transcripts, certificates, passport details, English language test results and any personal statements or references if needed.

Apply through the right channel. Many students from outside the EU apply directly via the university's international application portal. For some applicants you will use the Central Applications Office (CAO), so follow the instructions from the institution.
Monitor your application. Reply to requests for further documents and read any conditional offer carefully.
Accept your offer and arrange your funding.Please adhere to the payment and deposit instructions contained in your offer.
Prepare for your travel. If you are a student who requires a visa.

sections.title: Computer Engineering Accreditation and Recognition in Ireland
sections.lead: Accreditation is an important consideration when selecting an engineering degree.

items: Engineers Ireland accredits engineering programs to professional and academic standards. Accreditation can provide a form of professional development and can show that a program meets the recognized requirements for engineering education.
Review offer before accepting
Whether the program itself is accredited.
Accreditation covered qualification and program version.
If the accreditation is for the year you want to graduate.
How the qualification aligns with your plans for future professional registration.

The fact that a qualification is recognized does not mean that you will be guaranteed to be employed, registered or licensed in each country. If you intend to go back to India or work in another country, look into the requirements of the relevant employer, professional body or qualification recognition

faqs.q: What is the duration of a Computer Engineering degree in Ireland?
faqs.a: An undergraduate honors engineering degree usually takes four years, while some integrated engineering master's routes take five years. The length of a postgraduate degree alone depends on the program.

faqs.q: Is Computer Engineering offered under that course name in Ireland?
faqs.a: Not always. Other degrees covering similar subjects include Electronic and Computer Engineering, Computer and Communications Engineering or Electronic Engineering. Don't just compare the title of the course modules.

faqs.q: What are the tuition fees for international students?
faqs.a: The examples published for 2026/27 in this guide range from €17,900 per year at DCU for Year 1-4 to €27,640 per year at University of Galway for Electronic and Computer Engineering. These are institution-specific examples, not a universal range of fees. Living costs are separate.

faqs.q: What are the important subjects for admission?
faqs.a: Mathematics is especially important. You may also need physics and other science subjects for entry onto undergraduate courses. Postgraduate applicants usually need to have a relevant bachelor's degree and appropriate academic preparation.

faqs.q: What can I do after I graduate in Computer Engineering?
faqs.a: Graduates can be employed in embedded systems, computer hardware, firmware, electronics design, communications, robotics, semiconductor testing and other technical jobs. Your career success is dependent on the skills you have, your experience, the number of openings and your eligibility to be employed.
